newsitem.title: ITALY: ITALY SEEKS TELECOM ITALIA CORE INVESTORS.
newsitem.headline: ITALY SEEKS TELECOM ITALIA CORE INVESTORS.

text.p: The Italian Treasury said on Friday that letters had been sent to a number of investors who might be interested in joining a stable core of shareholders' in state telecom group Telecom Italia.
The Treasury said in a statement that its advisors for the forthcoming sale of stock in Telecom, Morgan Stanley and Euromobiliare, had sent the letters to "a limited list of potenital investors."
It said the companies involved offered "the required financial and/or business skills needed."
The state's 44 percent stake in Telecom Italia is due to be placed on the market in October.

The Treasury's statement said the government on Friday had introduced the already agreed decree that will allow Telecom to be sold both through a public flotation and also through a private placement to create the central core of shareholders.
No single company or investor will be able to take more than a three percent stake in the telecom giant.

Among firms that are believed to be interested in joining the stable core are U.S. telecommunications group AT&T, which earlier this year announced it was forming a strategic alliance with Telecom Italia.
Germany's Mannesmann has also been mentioned in the media as a potential investor.
Among Italian firms, the Agnelli holding IFIL and bank Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino SpA, are widely expected to join the inner-circle of key investors.
Italian banks Credito Italiano, Banca Commerciale Italiana and IMI are also believed to be interested.
